title: credential-prefetch-and-async-generator-ergonomics-bump
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Motivation: users report awkward ergonomics when combining credential prefetching with async generator based streaming in the TS SDK; parity gaps vs Go/Python lead to different failure modes under token rotation and transient network retries. This PR introduces a compact credential prefetch adaptor and ergonomic async-generator helpers that unify the lifecycle between TS/Go/Py SDKs while keeping backward-compatible call sites. Changes include: 1) CredentialPrefetcher: a small async factory that preloads short-lived tokens slightly early (configurable grace window) and exposes a lightweight lease object to the generator consumer so callers can opt into pinned credentials for critical sections. 2) AsyncGeneratorAdapter: two helpers (wrapAsyncGenerator and withPrefetch) that make it trivial to attach credential leases and deterministic retry hooks to existing streaming generators without changing upstream code shape. 3) Retry predicate enhancements: add a typed RetryHint returned by the adapter so callers can fine-tune backoff vs fast-fail semantics. 4) Cross-SDK parity shim: minimal API knobs added to the transport layer so Go/Py counterparts can match semantics in follow-up PRs. Compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior; new helpers are opt-in. Testing: unit tests for lease lifecycle, simulated token rotation, and end-to-end integration using the local mock transport. Also includes updates to docs and a migration note. Impact: small bundle size increase (+2KB gzipped) but meaningful reduction in stream-level race conditions during reauth and fewer transient 401 surface errors in internal canaries.
